criteria.description: Interactive 3D tabletop with identifiable puzzle parts
Ball moves on both ground-plane axes
Release produces observable coast and slowing
Ball and crate respect floor, walls and closed gate
Traversable ramp changes actual visible elevation
Physical contact moves the crate controllably
Gate depends on continuing crate occupancy
Opened route leads to a genuine victory
Loss and win restart restore all puzzle state
Ball, slope edges/heights, crate contact, pressure plate, gate state and exit are distinguishable during play.
Movement, plate condition, goal and loss/win restart controls are visible and match observed behavior.
Contact, plate on/off, gate open/closed, fall/loss and victory are visibly distinguishable.
Clean tabletop materials and scale are coherent, depth is legible and essential UI fits both viewports without obscuring the puzzle.
Observed delivery duration gated by demonstrated main-loop gameplay

limitations: Proposed engine-agnostic browser method; no maintainer acceptance or calibrated live-game judge is claimed.
Data-only protocol, not an executable Harbor task, creator adapter or automated recorder.
Evidence structure/arithmetic does not establish observation truth or authentic provenance.
Visible 3D behavior is assessed, not source-level engine implementation, exact physics or measured FPS.
Remote URLs can change; model labels and sampled delivery times are observations, not backend attestations.
Non-blind evaluation, platform defaults, missing data and all interventions must be disclosed.
Costs are reported separately; 60/10/30 totals are not historical Tetris scores or proof of equal task difficulty.
